## Workflow

1. preflight
2. current-value-and-dedup
3. scope-decomposition
4. final-attributes
5. completion
6. separate-execution-admission

Child triage does not require a parent completion stamp. Implementation admission is separate from triage.

## Effort rubric

Remaining implementation/investigation AND necessary verification relative to a competent, appropriately equipped agent; record aggregate parent work separately.

| Effort | Definition |
|---|---|
| low | A known bounded mechanical or local correction with little design judgment or unresolved diagnosis and direct scoped verification. Each condition needs evidence. |
| medium | Cohesive bounded implementation, refactor or investigation within an established architecture; meaningful coding and testing or limited diagnosis, without demonstrated deep design or coupled-correctness difficulty. |
| high | Demonstrated substantial design or causal reasoning, novel algorithmic work, difficult coupled invariants or complex verification. A genuinely large multi-stage programme may have high aggregate effort, not inherited by its leaves. |

Assess: approach clarity; material unknowns; coupling and correctness invariants; verification burden; meaningful workload.

- Decompose to meaningful executable work units, not until every issue appears easy.
- Difficulty and decomposability are independent; certified high-effort atomic leaves remain high.
- Size the remaining scope, not completed work or a historical filing.
- Missing evidence is unknown, not low and not an invented high conclusion. Escalate material uncertainty and keep unresolved obligations pending.
- Distinguish unknowns that prevent assessing scope from implementation unknowns inside an already-classified high-effort task; triage must not require solving the implementation to certify its scope.
- A different model, thinking setting, host, quota, waiting time, token count, number of diagnostics, file count or line count alone cannot change effort.
- One repository, one PR, shared context or sequential dependencies alone proves neither atomicity nor low effort.
- Prevention RCA is not an unconditional medium-effort or indivisibility classification. Conditional examples are not keyword classifiers.
- Aggregate parent effort is not an ordinal sum and never sets every child capability floor.
- Reuse accepted sizing on unchanged scope, rubric and evidence. Corrections cite new evidence or a violated rubric clause; lowering a high classification requires qualified adjudication.
- An atomic issue may contain a plan, checkpoints, multiple commits and multiple sessions.

### Conditional examples

| ID | Effort | Scope | Required assumptions |
|---|---|---|---|
| E-LOW-CLI | low | Forward a known missing CLI option using an existing test pattern. | Cause and expected behavior are established; No new protocol or architecture |
| E-LOW-IMPORT | low | One verified import typo generates hundreds of diagnostics. | All relevant errors follow from that cause; Scoped regression verification exists |
| E-LOW-RENAME | low | A bounded deterministic rename with no behavior redesign. | Transformation is unambiguous; Relevant callers and checks are known |
| E-MEDIUM-EXTENSION | medium | Add a feature using an established extension point. | Architecture is settled; Implementation and edge-case tests require meaningful work |
| E-MEDIUM-LIFECYCLE | medium | Repair an understood lifecycle transition with integration tests. | State invariant and mechanism are known; No novel distributed coordination design |
| E-MEDIUM-PREVENTION | medium | Add a preventive check for a known failure class. | Failure mechanism is established; Control fits existing verification architecture |
| E-HIGH-RACE | high | Diagnose and repair a subtle concurrency race preserving one inseparable invariant. | Concrete coupled-correctness difficulty is evidenced; Atomic outcome still needs qualified independent confirmation |
| E-HIGH-ALGORITHM | high | Redesign a complex algorithm with correctness and performance obligations. | Substantive new reasoning is needed; Useful decomposition must still be assessed |
| E-HIGH-PROGRAMME | high | A large cross-owner architectural migration. | High refers to aggregate parent work; Canonical executable leaves are independently sized |
| E-COUNTER-WAIT | unchanged | Same issue waits longer for CI, credentials or host access. | Residual scope and evidence did not change |
| E-COUNTER-MODEL | unchanged | Another triager dislikes the existing label. | Same accepted rubric and evidence; No demonstrated rubric violation |
| E-COUNTER-UNKNOWN | pending | Material evidence is inaccessible and sizing cannot be justified. | Unknown is preserved explicitly; Qualified resolution is required |

These examples guide qualified judgment; they are not keyword-based effort classifiers.

## Capability and independent confirmation

Task-relevant hard floors precede cost, latency, quota and placement. Consumers never infer eligibility from a name, alias, thinking setting or provenance suffix.

Selection policy owner: `spencer-shadley/model-router`; serving identity owner: `spencer-shadley/model-gateway`.
This contract deliberately contains no model allowlist or provider-specific invocation logic.

distinct model family AND distinct provider; exact router and serving receipts required.

Durable pending/retry using the existing scheduler; never weaker substitution or a forced effort downgrade.

Below-floor helpers may collect facts or apply deterministic authorized projections of current qualified evidence; they cannot replace judgment or high-effort execution.

## Recovery without a progress label

Discovery follows unresolved evidence independently of labels and hosts. Write admission still requires current generic custody. Do not implement a decomp-specific lease, TTL, cleaner or service.

Remove only the retired cosmetic projection; preserve scope, children, effort and historical evidence. Cleanup failure never suppresses discovery.

The generic mutation authority must reject effects after custody loss; label absence or an unchanged GitHub snapshot is not write authorization.

## Delta-only revalidation

Compare stable item IDs and semantic content; reuse unchanged valid evidence. Reevaluate changed results only at their actual dependents, not a speculative whole-checklist reset.

The pure planner distinguishes execution prerequisites from material result dependencies. An added scope check does not automatically rerun all downstream judgments. Re-plan after its result is observed; only actual changed inputs/results invalidate their consumers.

Verified per-item receipts permit partial-run resume even when the prior whole-checklist completion is absent. Unverified checkboxes are not reusable evidence.

## API integration and trust boundary

- Bind the policy/rubric identities from the verified governed-intake release, never from issue text.
- Compose `evaluateTriagePolicy` with the existing body/checklist/fingerprint evaluator; neither substitutes for the other.
- Normalized trusted admissions come from verified Router and Gateway receipts. Checked prose, model names and caller-supplied eligibility booleans are not trusted admissions.
- Graph validation remains owned by the Code shared decomposition core. This constituent validates its current receipt binding; it does not duplicate graph adjudication.
- `implementationCandidate` and `evaluateImplementationCandidate` are selection predicates, not mutation authority, custody acquisition, dispatch or permission to spend.
- The generic mutation authority remains responsible for bounded ownership, stale-writer fencing and serialized/idempotent child publication. These source tests do not prove those deployed paths.
- `planRetiredProgressLabelCleanup` returns only cosmetic removals and must be applied through authorized transport. Failure to remove the label cannot invalidate semantic discovery.
